intro: You're looking for a freelance bookkeeper near you — someone local who can take the stress out of your day-to-day financial admin. Whether you run a small business, work for yourself, or need help keeping on top of invoices and receipts, a freelance bookkeeper can offer flexible, personal support. We introduce you to a suitable UK bookkeeper who quotes you directly, with no obligation.
need_heading: What people searching for a freelance bookkeeper near me usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for a freelance bookkeeper near me want practical, local help with their bookkeeping, often because they're too busy to do it themselves or want to avoid costly mistakes.
needs: You run a small business and need someone to keep your records up to date so you can focus on running the business.
You're self-employed and want a local bookkeeper to help with invoices, expenses and preparing for your tax return.
You've fallen behind with your bookkeeping and need a freelance bookkeeper nearby to help you catch up.
You want to hand over the bookkeeping to someone who can offer a personal service and understand your situation.
You need a bookkeeper who can work flexibly around your schedule, perhaps visiting you or working remotely.
context_heading: What to understand about freelance bookkeepers
context: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct. So when you're looking for a freelance bookkeeper near you, it's worth checking these details.

A freelance bookkeeper often works for several small clients, offering flexibility and personal service. However, they should be clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice. Good bookkeepers will have professional indemnity insurance and will be happy to explain their data security practices.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Tell us the type of business you run or your employment status, as this affects the bookkeeping you need.
Let us know what bookkeeping tasks you need help with, such as invoicing, expenses, reconciliations or VAT.
Mention how far behind you are, if at all, so the bookkeeper can plan accordingly.
Tell us whether you prefer a bookkeeper who can visit you in person or one who works remotely.
Let us know if you have any specific software or systems you already use for your bookkeeping.
Tell us your rough timescales and any deadlines you're working towards, such as a tax return or year-end.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the freelance bookkeeper
questions: Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and by which body?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
What is your experience with businesses like mine?
How do you handle data security and confidentiality?
What are your arrangements for holiday cover or if you're unavailable?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's start, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice?

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper who is local to me?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many freelance bookkeepers work remotely and can serve clients anywhere. However, if you prefer face-to-face meetings or have documents to hand over, a local bookkeeper may be more convenient.

faqs.q: How do I check a freelance bookkeeper's credentials?
faqs.a: Ask whether they are supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes by HMRC or a professional body, and whether they hold professional indemnity insurance. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) indicates they have trained to a recognised standard.

faqs.q: Will a freelance bookkeeper also do my tax return?
faqs.a: Not usually. Bookkeepers focus on recording financial transactions, while tax returns and year-end accounts are typically handled by an accountant. A good bookkeeper will be clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before I contact a bookkeeper?
faqs.a: It helps to have an idea of your income and expenses, any software you use, and the tasks you need help with. Also think about whether you prefer someone local or remote, and any deadlines you're working towards.
